plan.title: Adipose treated vs control DE with sex/age covariates
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a single bulk RNA-seq experiment: /eval-full-32-with-covariates-n6-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples, raw integer gene-level counts from Salmon, gene symbols in the first column) with /eval-full-32-with-covariates-n6-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows: sample, condition, sex, age). Design is 6 treated vs 6 control human adipose samples, unpaired, one batch. The question — which genes differ between treated and control — is a two-group contrast, but the user states subjects differ in sex and are NOT age-matched, so an unadjusted contrast would confound treatment with age (and possibly sex). The plan therefore puts sex and age into the design formula as fixed effects (~ sex + age + condition) rather than regressing them out of the counts, which would exaggerate downstream confidence. T1S1 first quantifies how bad the imbalance actually is (age distribution by group, sex table by group, correlation of covariates with the leading PCs) and checks sample structure with a blind VST, PCA on the top 500 variable genes and a sample-distance heatmap — if age is nearly collinear with condition the adjusted model will have little residual power, and that must be stated up front rather than discovered in the results. T1S2 runs the DESeq2 Wald test on the adjusted design with a minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size), apeglm shrinkage of the condition_treated_vs_control coefficient, BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, and reports the unadjusted-vs-adjusted comparison so the size of the covariate effect is visible. T1S2b repeats the same design under edgeR quasi-likelihood as a robustness replicate; with 6 per group the two tools agree on most genes but not all, and the intersection is the high-confidence set. T2S1 takes the full ranked list of tested genes — ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic, the stated choice among the three defensible ranking metrics, because it scales effect by its uncertainty and does not saturate — into fgsea against the staged MSigDB human hallmark collection (2026.1) and then the staged Reactome human pathways, on the full list rather than a thresholded one. T1S3 consolidates: design, thresholds, MA and dispersion plots, p-value histogram, shrunken and unshrunken log2 fold changes with standard errors, the DESeq2/edgeR overlap, leading-edge genes per significant set, and the reproducibility record. Only 12 samples and 12,000 genes, so every step is small and CPU-light. The honest caveat carried through the whole plan: n=6 per group with two nuisance covariates leaves 8 residual degrees of freedom, and an age imbalance that the model adjusts for is still an imbalance — the result is an association under an assumed linear age effect, not a clean randomized contrast.

apeglm log fold change shrinkage on the condition_treated_vs_control coefficient
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same counts and design as a robustness replicate
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome
Consolidated report: design, thresholds, MA and dispersion plots, p-value histogram, shrunken and unshrunken LFC with lfcSE, DESeq2/edgeR overlap, leading-edge genes, sessionInfo

Gene set size window 15-500 applied after intersecting each set with the tested genes
Hallmark results reported first, Reactome results second, each with the collection name and version and each filtered to Homo sapiens
Share of tested gene symbols not matching the collection identifier space reported
Significant sets (BH < 0.05) reported with NES, adjusted p-value, set size, and leading-edge genes with their Wald statistics
Redundant sets collapsed into representatives with the full table retained as a supplement
Random seed set and recorded, since fgsea p-values are permutation-based
constraints: Rank on the Wald statistic; do not rank on the unshrunken log2 fold change alone and do not rank on a signed p-value
Use the full tested gene list as both the ranked input and, for any over-representation follow-up, the universe — never the whole genome or whole annotation
Filter the Reactome multi-species gene set file to Homo sapiens before testing
Do not run over-representation analysis if fewer than ~50 genes pass padj < 0.05; use the ranked result instead and say so
Do not fetch any gene set collection over the network; use only what the reference store provides
caveats: Enrichment results depend strongly on method and collection; report a set as a hypothesis for follow-up, not a proven finding
Long and highly expressed genes are easier to call significant, which biases set-level results; the ranked test on the full list mitigates but does not remove this
Nested and overlapping sets produce blocks of correlated hits; a count of significant sets overstates the number of independent findings

grounding.reason: Preranked fgsea on the full tested list is the default enrichment method (R-0107/R-0045); human order is Hallmark then Reactome (R-0048/R-0098). R-0108 is disputed — the plan chooses the DESeq2 Wald statistic as the ranking metric, per R-0099.

steps.name: Consolidated differential expression report
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to 'which genes differ between treated and control adipose samples', given n=6 per group, mixed sex, and unmatched age?
steps.description: Assemble one report from T1S1, T1S2, T1S2b and T2S1. It must state: the method and the version of every package; the design formula ~ sex + age + condition, the explicit reference level (control) and the contrast direction (treated vs control); the significance thresholds; the number of genes tested after filtering and the number called differentially expressed. Include the MA plot and the dispersion plot as the two fit diagnostics, placed before the gene tables, each with a sentence on what it shows, plus the p-value histogram from T1S2. The gene table carries, per gene, the unshrunken log2 fold change, the apeglm-shrunken log2 fold change, lfcSE, stat, pvalue and padj, with genes ranked and plotted on the shrunken value and the shrinkage estimator named in the header. Report the DESeq2/edgeR overlap from T1S2b as the high-confidence set. For enrichment, give the collection and its version, the ranking metric, the universe, the size window, and the leading-edge genes of each significant set, with the caveat that enrichment results are method-dependent. Close with the confounding assessment from T1S1 restated in plain terms — how imbalanced age was, what adjusting for it cost in power, and how the unadjusted sensitivity fit differed — and attach the reproducibility record (sessionInfo, seeds, package versions, gene set collection versions).
steps.context: This is the deliverable that answers the research question. It must not overstate: 12 samples, two nuisance covariates, an acknowledged age imbalance, and no external validation cohort.
acceptance_criteria: Method, package versions, design formula, reference level, contrast, thresholds, n tested and n DE all stated before the gene tables
MA plot, dispersion plot and p-value histogram included, each with a one-line reading
Gene table carries unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj; ranking and plots use the shrunken value and name apeglm
DESeq2/edgeR intersection reported as the high-confidence set, with method-specific genes listed separately
Enrichment section names collection, version, ranking metric (Wald statistic), universe, size window, and lists leading-edge genes per significant set
Confounding assessment restated: age imbalance magnitude, adjusted vs unadjusted comparison, and an explicit statement that the result is an adjusted association, not a randomized contrast
Reproducibility record (sessionInfo, seeds, package and collection versions) attached to the output rather than kept separately
constraints: Do not rank or headline genes by the unshrunken log2 fold change
Do not report the union of DESeq2 and edgeR calls as the result
State the number of significant genes even when it is zero or very small; do not relax the threshold to produce a longer list
Do not claim mechanism or causality from an enrichment hit
caveats: With 6 per group and two covariates, confidence intervals on fold changes are wide; effect sizes should be read as estimates with substantial uncertainty
Adjusting for an imbalanced covariate does not restore the comparison a matched design would have given
No independent validation cohort is available in this dataset; all findings are internal

grounding.reason: Report contents follow the reporting rules returned for this situation: method/versions/design/thresholds (R-0041), shrunken and unshrunken LFC with lfcSE (R-0085), MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087), two-method overlap (R-0042), enrichment provenance and method-dependence caveat (R-0051/R-0055), leading edge per set (R-0105), reproducibility record (R-0086).
